newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia shares end down on drop in bank earnings.
newsitem.headline: Colombia shares end down on drop in bank earnings.

text.p: Colombian shares ended mostly lower in trading that saw leading indices dragged down by sales of stock in Banco de Colombia.

The bank, Colombia's second largest in terms of assets, has been under selling pressure since last Friday when it announced it had given up on efforts to form a strategic partnership with Spain's Banco Central Hispano-Americano.

It shed 2.85 percent in Bogota Wednesday, falling to a historic low of 274 pesos per share, after it announced a drop of more than 60 percent in its first-quarter earnings compared with the same period a year ago.
The lower-than-expected earnings report drove Banco de Colombia even lower in Medellin, where brokers said a selling frenzy pushed it down 3.51 percent to 371.5 pesos per share.
Bank officials were set to hold a conference call with investors in New York on Thursday in an apparent bid to restore confidence, but some brokers said it may be too late.
"The bank has sacrificed too much in terms of profits and shareholder dividends," said one broker, who added it faced an uphill battle in clearing up its past due loan portfolio.
An increase in past due loan provisions was one of the reasons for Colombia's poor first-quarter performance.

Other movers included Banco de Bogota, flagship of the Luis Carlos Sarmiento conglomerate. It fell 1.06 percent to end at 6,380 pesos per share on what brokers described as profit- taking and a lack of demand from foreign investment funds.
The same was said of brewing giant Bavaria, which slipped 0.63 percent to close at 7,800 pesos per share.
The day's few gainers were led by cement maker Cementos Argos, which ended up 3.40 percent at 8,531 pesos per share on market talks of strong first-quarter earnings.
